390
# Harness: the engine_sync device keeps folders the user makes at a name the rules leave out on its disk unseen, refuses each effect that would put an entry at such a name, retries blocked effects once the run goes quiet as the driver's retry timer does, and accepts a node that stays blocked only where no conflict name is allowed. Before this, engine_sync never refused an effect, so it could not reach the shape this PR fixes.
# Harness: the sent-move check accepts an unmarked Move only when the device holds a record that its disk refused R's name for the node and the Move is made over the live place R holds. A unit test pins each direction: with the record it passes, and without the record, with R trashed, with R elsewhere, or without from it is flagged. The existing sent-move tests cover only moves the disk already shows and pending marks.
# Generator: a property test moves a node onto a folder the rules leave out with random changes around it, so the record-keyed exemption runs on generated cases. It found the parked-file case this PR also fixes.
# Sim: another device's delete or rename after the refusal is recorded wins, whether this device hears it before it commits or not. No existing test changes the node on the server while a refusal record is held.
# Harness: the settle checks hold a blocked effect or a parked node to the refusals the record covers: a blocked effect that puts a node at the exact place R holds must wait on a left-out folder with no conflict name allowed, and a place a left-out folder holds on the disk counts as one no node reaches. Without this, battery cases where a parked file's own name is held by such a folder fail checks the record was never meant to clear.
# Sim: a conflict rename in flight when the rules let its name back in still finishes; the rules are lifted before each step of the commit. No existing test lifts a rule while a conflict rename is in flight.
# Commit: a second user move back to the old synced name must still be sent after a guarded resend is acknowledged. Separately, a sent conflict rename's record survives a server deletion and a local placement until the answer.
# Sim: a refused remote name still gets a conflict copy when the parked file's old local name is left out. The earlier parked-file test uses an included local name.
# Commit: a conflict rename in a commit dropped unanswered is sent again while R holds the node at the place it was sent over, and its record ends when R moved the node meanwhile. No existing test drops the commit that carries a conflict rename.
# Store: an abandoned engine state load stops while it reads the refused-name records, as every other engine state reader does. No existing abandoned-read test fills names_left_out.
